subjective.question: (Marks: 2) What type of computer is suitable for mobile use and why?
subjective.answer: These are known as mobile computers. They are small in size and easy to carry. They have internet and other accessories on them, so that we can easily get access to the internet.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) What type of computer is suitable for larger organizations and why?
subjective.answer: Mainframe computer is suitable for large organizations, as they are dealing with a large amount of data and need to process it in a centralized way, so it is suitable for large organizations.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) What is the difference between closing and exiting?
subjective.answer: Closing removes the particular part of the program (the document/file) if it is used on the main screen or window — close only closes the document, not the software, e.g. Microsoft Word, Excel, etc. Whereas exit means to close the file and also to exit (close) the whole application/software.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) What is an Icon?
subjective.answer: The image of software normally appearing on the desktop is called an icon. Icons allow us to access software directly by double-clicking on the required software.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) Is it possible to switch among multiple documents? How can we switch using the keyboard?
subjective.answer: Yes, it is possible to switch among multiple documents by using Alt+Tab.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) How to select multiple files?
subjective.answer: For selecting multiple files, first we select one file and then, holding Ctrl, we select the other files. In this way we can select multiple files in a folder.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) Write steps to open a Notepad.
subjective.answer: 1. From START MENU we will move to ALL PROGRAMS. 2. From ALL PROGRAMS, we will move to ACCESSORIES. 3. From ACCESSORIES, we will move to NOTEPAD.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) Define standard and status bars.
subjective.answer: Standard Bar: A standard bar contains icons for functions such as file management, printing, editing, formatting and calculating. It is located just below the menu bar in an application window. Status Bar: A horizontal line of information displayed at the bottom of an application window. It reports information about the current status of the program or the data contents in the window.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) What does Undo do?
subjective.answer: This command allows us to undo things. For example, during typing we removed some stuff and want it back; if we press Ctrl+Z, we will get all the stuff back in the same position.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) Use Word to create the bulleted text as shown below (the simple text for creating the bulleted text is also given) and paste the bulleted text in your answer area.
subjective.answer: i. CPL Environment • Introduction ii. Input • Keyboard Basics — There are many types of keyboards but normally we use standard keyboards having 104 keys, and they can be separated as follows: Numeric Pad, Alphabetic Pad, Function Keys, Cursor Portion. • Pointing Devices — Mouse, mouse pad iii. Output • Types of Output — 2 types • Categories of Output • Output Devices — Monitor, Printer, Plotter

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) How can we delete cell contents?
subjective.answer: Click the cell and press the Delete key from the keyboard.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) How can we modify column widths and row heights?
subjective.answer: Method 1 (dragging): Place the mouse on the edge of the grid of the column or row. The pointer will change its shape; drag the pointer to adjust the width/height. Method 2 (menu): Column width — select the column and right-click the mouse; there is an option of Column Width, click on it and it will show the current width of the column; put your required width in it. The same way can be used for one column or all columns. Row height — select the rows you want to change, right-click at the border area of the rows; there is an option of Row Height. Click on it, it will show the current height of the rows; there you can put the required height of the row you need.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) Describe the function of the following shortcut keys in PowerPoint: CTRL+Y, CTRL+N, CTRL+O, CTRL+W, CTRL+S, ALT+F4.
subjective.answer: CTRL+Y — To redo an action that has just been undone. CTRL+N — It creates a new presentation window. CTRL+O — This opens a search browser to open a saved file in the computer. CTRL+W — Close the slides. CTRL+S — Save. ALT+F4 — Close (the application).

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) How can we insert clip art in a PowerPoint presentation?
subjective.answer: Select the clip, copy it with CTRL+C and paste it on the PowerPoint slide with CTRL+V.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) What is slide layout? Is there any way to change the default layout of the slide? If yes, then explain in your own words.
subjective.answer: The slide layout in PowerPoint is the arrangement of all the items that make up your slide, such as title, graphics or text boxes. Yes, we can change the default layout. To modify the layout, first go to the View tab and then click on the Slide Master button. Then click on the first slide; changes that you make to this slide will be used by the other layout slides shown below the slide master. Use all of the tools on the tab to set the dimensions, theme and background styles for your slides. When you have finished this, click in the title text box and use the tools in the Drawing Tools Format tab and the Home tab in order to modify the style of your text. Next, click on the contents text box and change the styles for the different levels of text.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) What is slide transition? What is the method of adding a transition in PowerPoint slides?
subjective.answer: Slide transition is the effect/movement between slides in a presentation. Because of transition we don't need to click with the mouse to go to the next slide. When we need to give a presentation, we can select the auto time on it; the difference between the slides could be 10 seconds. We go to Animations, and there we can find transition.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) How can we bookmark a web page?
subjective.answer: To bookmark a web page in Internet Explorer, select the "Bookmarks" option and click "Save" in the drop-down menu. Save, edit or add a bookmark to a web browser to find a site quickly on the Internet. It is located in the location bar of Internet Explorer.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) How can we delete a bookmark?
subjective.answer: Go to Favorites, bring the mouse pointer on the bookmark you want to delete and press the Delete key from the keyboard.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) How can we mark a message as unread / read?
subjective.answer: Read: Go to the message and click on it. Unread: Click on the message, open it, and there is an option of "make it unread"; click on it.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) a. What is electronic mailing? Give its basic concept and usage. b. What are computer viruses?
subjective.answer: a. Electronic mail, also written as E-mail, is an electronic transmission of messages, letters and documents. It includes point-to-point services in which a text file that is sent or received can be edited. The basic concept of E-mail is to send and receive messages as quickly as possible, with the addition of sounds, graphics, links, etc., which can never be possible through the old postage system, as that took long and also had to go through country borders. For using e-mail, both persons — sender and receiver — have to have a computer to read it or send it. The sender composes an e-mail by clicking on Compose Mail, writes the receiver's e-mail address in the To field, types the message and sends it to the receiver's computer. Usage: It is the fastest way of communication in the world; businessmen are using the benefits of e-mail; its cost is very low; it is quick and fast. E-mail typically is used for conversations that are not urgent and for dialogues that are expected to continue over a period of time. The structure of e-mail eliminates interruptions associated with telephone conversations or electronic pagers. It also permits asynchronous communication, which can benefit both the sender and the recipient in our busy society. b. A computer virus is a computer program that can copy itself and infect a computer. The term "virus" is also commonly but mistakenly used to refer to other types of malware, including but not limited to adware and spyware programs that do not have the reproductive ability. Viruses can increase their chances of spreading to other computers by infecting files on a network file system or a file system that is accessed by another computer. Example: Trojan horses. It is software which is developed to kill/damage Windows; it can damage the hardware; it puts a negative effect on computer and internet speed.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) Differentiate between hardware and software. Give two examples of each. Which one is intangible?
subjective.answer: Hardware is the physical part of the computer that we can touch, e.g. monitor, keyboard, hard disk and mouse. Software is the set of instructions/programs that tells the hardware what to do; it cannot be touched, e.g. MS Word and Windows. Software is intangible, while hardware is tangible.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) What is primary storage? How does it differ from secondary storage? Give examples of each.
subjective.answer: Primary storage (main memory) is the memory directly used by the CPU while the computer is working; it is temporary (volatile) and faster, e.g. RAM. Secondary storage is used to store data and programs permanently; it is non-volatile and slower but has much larger capacity, e.g. hard disk, floppy disk and optical disk (CD/DVD).

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) Write the steps to save a file as a web page in MS Word.
subjective.answer: 1. Open the document in MS Word. 2. Click File and choose "Save as Web Page" (File > Save as Webpage). The document is saved in web page (HTML) format, which can be opened in a web browser.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) What is a spreadsheet? Name the three types of data found in a spreadsheet.
subjective.answer: A spreadsheet is a program (such as MS Excel) used to organize, calculate and analyze data in rows and columns. The three types of data found in a spreadsheet are: (1) Numbers (values/constants), (2) Formulas (used for calculations), and (3) Labels (text/words).

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) What is a cell in MS Excel? How is a cell address formed, and how is the active cell identified?
subjective.answer: The intersection of a row and a column in a worksheet is called a cell. A cell address is formed by the column letter followed by the row number, e.g. C4 means column C, row 4 (an absolute address is written with dollar signs, e.g. $C$4). The cell currently selected for data entry is the active cell, and it is identified by a dark wide (heavy) border around it.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) Differentiate between a workbook and a worksheet. How can a worksheet be removed (deleted) from a workbook?
subjective.answer: A workbook is the complete Excel file, which contains one or more worksheets. A worksheet (sheet) is a single page of rows and columns inside the workbook where data is entered. To remove a worksheet: right-click on the sheet tab of the spreadsheet and select DELETE.

subjective.question: (Marks: 2) Which button on the Standard toolbar gives quick access to the SUM, AVERAGE, COUNT, MIN and MAX functions? What is this feature called?
subjective.answer: The AutoSum button on the Standard toolbar gives quick access to the Sum, Average, Count, Min and Max functions. This feature is called AutoSum.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) What is a chart in MS Excel? Which chart type is used to show the pattern or relationships between sets of data points, and which keyboard shortcut creates a chart from the selected data?
subjective.answer: A chart is the graphical representation of worksheet data, created in Excel with the Chart Wizard. The XY (Scatter) chart shows the pattern or relationships between sets of data points (a Pie chart, in contrast, shows proportions of a whole). The keyboard shortcut to create a chart from the selected cells/data is F11.

subjective.question: (Marks: 5) What is the World Wide Web (WWW)? How is it different from the Internet? What is a URL?
subjective.answer: The World Wide Web (WWW) is a part of the Internet: it is the collection of web pages and web sites that are accessed through web browsers. The Internet is the worldwide network of computers itself, while the Web is one of the services that runs on the Internet (e-mail is another service). A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) is the address of a specific document or resource on the WWW, e.g. www.vu.edu.pk.

subjective.question: (Marks: 3) What is encryption? Why is it used, and what is a secure site?
subjective.answer: Encryption is the process of converting readable data into unreadable characters (coded form) to prevent unauthorized use; only the authorized receiver can decrypt (decode) it back into readable form. A secure site is a web site that uses encryption techniques to secure its data.

subjective.question: What does the term "system unit" encompass?
subjective.answer: The system unit encapsulates the processor, motherboard, CD drives, hard drives, memory, ports, etc.

subjective.question: What is the primary function of a motherboard in a computer?
subjective.answer: The motherboard holds together the central processing unit (CPU), memory, and connectors for input and output devices.

subjective.question: What is the processor, and what is its role in a computer?
subjective.answer: The processor is the brain of the computer and is responsible for all processing tasks.

subjective.question: Can hardware function without software?
subjective.answer: No, hardware does not work without software.

subjective.question: Describe RAM, and why is it considered volatile memory?
subjective.answer: RAM stands for Random Access Memory. It is temporary and volatile memory because it loses all information when the power is off.

subjective.question: Why are secondary storage devices needed? What are their advantages?
subjective.answer: Secondary storage devices are needed because RAM stores information temporarily, and ROM cannot store user information; they are non-volatile storage devices. Their advantages are that more data can be stored compared to primary storage devices, and information remains saved even if the power is switched off.

subjective.question: What are toggle keys? Name three toggle keys.
subjective.answer: Toggle keys are the keys that switch a feature on or off. The three toggle keys are Caps Lock, Num Lock and Scroll Lock. They have corresponding lights on the keyboard to show their status.

subjective.question: What is the primary function of an operating system?
subjective.answer: An operating system manages and coordinates the activities of computer hardware and other software.

subjective.question: Differentiate between utility software and application software.
subjective.answer: Utility software performs tasks like maintenance, troubleshooting, and virus scanning. Application software helps with daily life tasks like calculation, presentation, and text editing.

subjective.question: How can hardware theft be prevented?
subjective.answer: Hardware theft can be prevented by keeping the hardware/computer safe from stealing, e.g. by placing it somewhere safe and secure.

subjective.question: How does antivirus software protect a computer?
subjective.answer: Antivirus software is used to eliminate viruses from a computer. It scans the hard disk to find and terminate viruses, preventing new ones from entering.

subjective.question: How can unauthorized access to computer data be reduced?
subjective.answer: Unauthorized access can be reduced by protecting your computer/data with a password.

subjective.question: Why is data backup important?
subjective.answer: Data saved in a computer may be lost for various reasons. Having a backup allows access and use of the data in case of loss or damage.

subjective.question: What is a printer? Name two types of printers.
subjective.answer: A printer is an output device that prints text or images stored in the computer, producing a hard copy. Two types of printers are the dot matrix printer and the line printer.

subjective.question: Write the steps to save a file on a floppy disk.
subjective.answer: 1. Insert the floppy disk into the floppy drive. 2. Open the file and choose File > Save As. 3. Select the floppy drive (A:) as the save location. 4. Type the file name and click Save.

subjective.question: What is the purpose of Windows Explorer?
subjective.answer: Windows Explorer allows users to browse folders and files on the computer, providing a convenient way to manage and access data.

subjective.question: How do you create a new folder on the desktop?
subjective.answer: Right-click on the empty area of the desktop and select "New" > "Folder".

subjective.question: How can you delete a file or folder?
subjective.answer: Right-click on the file or folder and choose "Delete", drag it to the Recycle Bin, or select it and press the "Delete" key on the keyboard.

subjective.question: What is the purpose of the Recycle Bin? How can deleted files be recovered from it?
subjective.answer: The Recycle Bin contains deleted files and folders. Files can be restored from the Recycle Bin, but once deleted from the Recycle Bin, they cannot be recovered. To recover a file, open the Recycle Bin, click on the file, and then click "Restore this item" on the toolbar. To restore all items, ensure no files are selected and click "Restore all items".

subjective.question: What are the two types of scroll bars in a window?
subjective.answer: The two types of scroll bars are: 1) Vertical scroll bar, used to scroll the window up and down. 2) Horizontal scroll bar, used to scroll the window left and right.

subjective.question: How can you identify the active window?
subjective.answer: The active window has a dark-colored title bar, while inactive windows have light-colored title bars.

subjective.question: How can we create a desktop icon (shortcut) on the desktop?
subjective.answer: Right-click on an empty area of the desktop, select "New" and then "Shortcut". Browse and select the file or program, click Next, and then click Finish. (A shortcut can also be created by right-clicking the file and choosing "Send to > Desktop (create shortcut)".)

subjective.question: How is a word processor different from a basic text editor?
subjective.answer: A word processor is a complex (advanced) form of text editor that provides basic text-editing functionality along with features like spell and grammar checkers.

subjective.question: What is the purpose of the "Find and Replace" feature in MS Word?
subjective.answer: The "Find and Replace" feature allows you to find specific words or phrases in a document and replace them with other text.

subjective.question: How can you insert special characters and symbols in MS Word?
subjective.answer: From the Insert tab, click on "Symbol" and select the desired symbol from the drop-down menu. More symbols and special characters can be accessed by clicking on "More Symbols".

subjective.question: What are templates in MS Word?
subjective.answer: Templates are pre-designed and styled document samples provided by MS Word. They can be accessed through the File tab, and users can choose a suitable template for their needs.

subjective.question: What is the significance of the green wavy line in MS Word?
subjective.answer: The green wavy line represents a grammatical mistake. It suggests revising the fragment from a grammar perspective.

subjective.question: What does a soft copy refer to in the context of document printing?
subjective.answer: A soft copy is a file created using software and saved on a computer.

subjective.question: Why do we use mail merge?
subjective.answer: Mail merge is used to merge information with letters, preparing them for delivery, whether as postal mail or electronic mail.

subjective.question: What are the basic steps of mail merge?
subjective.answer: The basic steps of mail merge involve preparing the letter or invitation (main document), creating a list of recipients, and merging the information from the list into the main letter.

subjective.question: What does ISP stand for, and what is its role?
subjective.answer: ISP stands for Internet Service Provider. It connects users to the Internet and provides them Internet access.

subjective.question: What is an email address?
subjective.answer: An email address is the address used to send emails from one computer to another, e.g. info@vu.edu.pk.
